metadata.title: NHRA Medicine Licensing Guideline
metadata.edition: Version 4.2, document control 21.01.2026 · section 3: MAH responsible for safety through the life cycle and for notifying NHRA of new significant safety information; no pharmacovigilance section
metadata.legal_basis: NHRA guideline under the medicine registration regulation (Decree No. (32) of 2020); the regulation prevails.
metadata.applicability: Applicants, sponsors and market authorization holders reporting ICSRs (see the PV Info ICSR rulebook for scope).

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.statement: NHRA National Health Regulatory Authority. Package Leaflet (PL) The package leaflet is the medicine information provided in the pack. It should be drawn up in accordance with the summary of the product characteristics.
candidates.context: Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH) The pharmaceutical company that legally holds the right and responsibility of marketing the medicine in Bahrain. PPR Pharmacy & Pharmaceutical Product Regulation is the responsible department for medicine licensing at NHRA.

candidates.statement: Introduction Guideline documents are meant to provide assistance to industry and professionals on how to comply with governing statutes and regulations. Guideline documents also provide assistance to staff on how NHRA mandates and objectives should be implemented in a manner that is fair, consistent, and effective.
candidates.context: Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) The definitive description of the product. The SmPC is an integral part of the marketing authorization. This guideline has been developed to assist license holders in the preparation and submission of applications for licensing medicines in the Kingdom of Bahrain.

candidates.context: It should be noted that the NHRA has the right to request any further information and data. 1. Scope This guidance document describes the procedures and requirements for submission of an application to obtain a new medicine license in the Kingdom of Bahrain.

candidates.statement: 2. Medicine Licensing Any medicine must be licensed before marketing in Bahrain as per decree-law # (18) of 1997 amended by decree-law # (20) of 2015, and in accordance with the resolution (63) of 2019 (on NHRA website).
candidates.context: Applicants are expected to comply with the procedures and requirements laid out in this guidance. Medicine importation and distribution must be done through authorized pharmacy only (Local agent), this agent can be the applicant on behalf of the pharmaceutical company if the agreement is prone to NHRA and acknowledged.

candidates.context: Medicine importation and distribution must be done through authorized pharmacy only (Local agent), this agent can be the applicant on behalf of the pharmaceutical company if the agreement is prone to NHRA and acknowledged. Pharmaceutical companies (MAH) should note that they are responsible for the medicine’s quality, efficacy, and safety throughout its life cycle. Responsibility starts with the licensing of the medicine and ends when the medicine license is cancelled. Since the medicine quality, efficacy and safety can change at any time during the course of its life cycle, it is the MAH responsibility to inform NHRA when these changes occur as per the current guidelines.
